newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on mkt liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on mkt liquidity.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed down 75 basis points on Thursday at 17.90 percent after liquidity pressures eased from the prior session, traders said.
"The market was quiet and stable, and trended downwards," a fixed-income analyst said.
The analyst said upside pressure eased after banks had to settle balances outstanding on checking accounts they heold with the central bank on Wednesday.
"It was partly because the cutoff date is out of the way and we also saw foreign capital inflow, which can be seen from the exchange rate," he said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts reversed early weakness and closed unchanged at 7.8925/7.8960 per dollar.
Dealers noted that a late recovery in U.S. long bonds also paved the way for Cetes rates to decline. The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was up 7/32 to yield 6.87 percent.
"Long bond yields eased a little and that helped government rates to fall," a dealer said.
One analyst said market stability was also bolstered by Banco de Mexico's announcement it would now allow banks to have equal short and long positions in their final balance after each day's trading.
Previously, banks were allowed to close each day with short positions equivalent to three times long positions held.
"The new measure, which basically allows banks to have a greater overdraft, also stabilized the market," a trader said.
The central bank drained 2.514 billion pesos from the market through three direct Cetes sales and three repos.
Overnight rates on bank paper closed down 40 basis points at 19.15 percent.
Cetes futures closed up five centavos to 78.65 pesos for June contrcts traded on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
Liquidity of 1.178 billion pesos was due to return to the market on Friday from prior central bank participation.
